title: A user removed from a project can no longer read that project's compliance map data even with a valid org role
description: requireProjectMembership() gates every /projects/:projectId/* route in compliance-frameworks.routes.js and client-compliance.routes.js. Regression guard for the pre-PLAC state where these controllers only ever called assertOrgAccess (org-membership), never real project membership.
preconditions: User held ProjectMember row on project P, now removed
User's org role still grants compliance.read at the org level
User is not an org-level project.admin
expectedResult: All four requests return 403 Forbidden. Org-level compliance.read is not sufficient once project membership is revoked.

title: A non-super-admin cannot read another organization's frameworks via the organizationId query/path param
preconditions: organizationId in the request path belongs to org B
steps: As an org A user, call GET /compliance-frameworks/organizations/<orgB-id>/frameworks
expectedResult: 403 Forbidden — listByOrganization's scopedOrgId-vs-organizationId mismatch check rejects the request before any org B data is queried.

title: Calling the activation API directly for an unlicensed framework is rejected server-side even if the UI gate is bypassed
description: Confirms the licensing check in addToProject is enforced independently of the frontend's Upgrade Required modal — a scripted/direct API call must not be able to activate an unlicensed framework.
preconditions: Framework X is not in the org's licensed set
steps: As an authenticated user with compliance.create, POST /compliance-frameworks/projects/:projectId/frameworks with { frameworkId: X } directly (bypassing the UI)
expectedResult: 403 { success:false, error:'LICENSING_REQUIRED' }. No ClientFramework record is created and complianceSync.activateFramework is never invoked.

title: excludedRequirementIds cannot be used to mark another framework's or another project's controls Not Applicable
description: updateExcludedControls validates every candidate ID against FrameworkRequirement scoped to cf.frameworkId — an attacker-supplied requirement ID belonging to a different framework (even one the org has never activated) is filtered out server-side.
preconditions: Framework F1 is active for project P
A valid, active leaf requirement ID R2 belongs to an unrelated framework F2
steps: PATCH /compliance-frameworks/projects/P/frameworks/:id/excluded-controls with excludedRequirementIds: [R2] where :id is F1's ClientFramework record
expectedResult: The response's excludedRequirementIds array does not contain R2 — F1's ClientFramework document cannot reference F2's requirements.

title: CSV export sanitises formula-injection prefixes on control/resource titles before writing cells
description: exportCSV()'s sanitise() helper prefixes any cell value starting with =, +, -, @, tab or CR with a leading apostrophe, preventing a maliciously-named control/resource title (e.g. from an AI-generated or vendor-supplied title) from executing as a formula when the export is opened in Excel/Sheets.
preconditions: A resource attached to a control has a title of '=1+1' (or begins with +, -, @)
steps: Export the compliance map to CSV including this resource
Inspect the raw CSV file content for that cell
expectedResult: The cell is written as "'=1+1" (leading apostrophe preserved in the raw file) — not a bare '=1+1' that a spreadsheet application would evaluate as a formula on open.

title: Bulk control/check status endpoints require framework.admin, not the lesser framework.read/update permissions
description: PATCH /:frameworkId/controls/bulk-status and /:frameworkId/checks/bulk-status are gated on requirePermission('framework.admin') — a user who only has framework.update (enough to edit a single control) must not be able to mass-toggle an entire framework's controls/checks.
preconditions: User has framework.read and framework.update but NOT framework.admin
expectedResult: 403 Forbidden — framework.update alone does not unlock the bulk endpoints; no controls are modified.

title: A 403 on the framework.read-gated getFramework call degrades the compliance map header only, without exposing coverage data it shouldn't have gated
description: FrameworkComplianceMap.jsx deliberately fetches getFramework (framework.read) separately from getClientRequirements/getClientFrameworkCoverage (compliance.read) so a role with compliance.read but not framework.read still sees coverage data, just with a degraded header. Confirms the split doesn't leak framework.read-only fields (e.g. internal region/version metadata) through the compliance.read-gated endpoints as a side-channel.
preconditions: User has compliance.read but NOT framework.read
steps: Observe the header area and the coverage/control data
expectedResult: An info banner reads that framework details (title/version/region) couldn't be loaded due to missing permission, while coverage stats and the control list still render normally. GET /compliance-frameworks/:id (framework.read-gated) itself still returns 403 for this user.
